aspect_adaptations: memory_ownership is read as result-set, work_mem and spill discipline (the engine owns allocation; the guide's job is bounding what materializes server-side, on the wire and client-side); concurrency is read as PostgreSQL transaction isolation, MVCC snapshot semantics and lock discipline.

assertions_contracts.best_practice: Matches PostgreSQL's documented constraint semantics, which are unchanged in 18; constraints firing on every write path is the documented reason to prefer them over application checks.
assertions_contracts.evidence: PostgreSQL 18's release line (18.6, 2026-08-13) contains no constraint-model change that affects this section.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Constraints are the assertion system: NOT NULL by default, named CHECK/UNIQUE/foreign-key constraints, EXCLUSION constraints and partial unique indexes for rules plain constraints cannot state; the CHECK-evaluates-to-UNKNOWN caveat is handled by pairing with NOT NULL; large-table constraint adds go NOT VALID then validate in bounded batches.

bounded_work.best_practice: Stricter than any official default, and nothing in PostgreSQL 18 contradicts it; the timeout settings and keyset pattern are the documented mechanisms.
bounded_work.evidence: No contradicting official position in the PostgreSQL 18 documentation or the 2026-08-13 update announcement.
bounded_work.guide_position: LIMIT with a named maximum plus deterministic ORDER BY on unbounded tables, keyset pagination instead of OFFSET at scale, bounded batches for bulk writes, statement_timeout/lock_timeout/idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on serving sessions, capped IN lists and array parameters.

concurrency.best_practice: This is PostgreSQL's documented MVCC and locking model, stated accurately including the anomaly/retry trade-offs of each level.
concurrency.evidence: PostgreSQL 18's asynchronous I/O changes execution mechanics, not the isolation or locking contract this section teaches.
concurrency.guide_position: Isolation level chosen deliberately: READ COMMITTED per-statement snapshot semantics stated, REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE paired with whole-transaction bounded retry on 40001/40P01, deliberate FOR UPDATE / FOR NO KEY UPDATE with NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED only where its semantics fit, one documented lock order, long transactions treated as a vacuum/bloat hazard, namespaced advisory locks.

error_handling.best_practice: Matches PostgreSQL's documented transaction-failure semantics exactly.
error_handling.evidence: No change in the 18 line alters the aborted-transaction model or the SQLSTATE classes cited.
error_handling.guide_position: Any error aborts the transaction (25P02 until rollback); errors handled by SQLSTATE class at the interpreting boundary (23505 as a designed race outcome, 23514/23502 as bugs); serialization failures and deadlocks retry the whole transaction, never a fragment; savepoints and PL/pgSQL exception blocks carry an explicit cost warning.

formatting.best_practice: A single pinned formatter whose output wins is current practice for sqruff, and sqruff's connection-free LSP/formatter split from the database-backed language server is the project's documented usage.
formatting.evidence: The formatter choice and configuration story check out against the sqruff project; the version number claimed for it is assessed under toolchain_pins because it could not be independently confirmed.
formatting.guide_position: sqruff is the one formatter and lint gate (sqruff fix / sqruff lint), dialect pinned in .sqruff, version recorded with the toolchain, generated SQL exempt and marked; postgres-language-server's own formatter is explicitly not used so 'formatted' has one meaning.

memory_ownership.best_practice: Matches PostgreSQL's documented memory model (work_mem multiplication across operations and connections is the documented hazard).
memory_ownership.evidence: Nothing in PostgreSQL 18 changes the work_mem or materialization model this section describes.
memory_ownership.guide_position: work_mem is per sort/hash operation, not per query or connection, and is raised only per-session with SET LOCAL; result sets materialize server-side, on the wire and client-side so row bounds keep all three finite; COPY or bounded multi-row inserts for bulk load; routine temp spilling treated as a design defect.

security.best_practice: This is PostgreSQL's documented security posture - the documentation's own warning that SECURITY DEFINER functions must pin search_path is the guide's rule in substance.
security.evidence: No PostgreSQL 18 security change (including its new authentication options) weakens or replaces any rule here.
security.guide_position: Parameterize every runtime value with no exceptions; dynamic identifiers only from a server-side allowlist quoted with format('%I')/quote_ident; least-privilege roles (app role holds no DDL, ownership or superuser); row-level security as defense in depth; SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path; secrets kept out of statement text because logs and pg_stat_statements retain it; COPY TO PROGRAM and server-side file access are superuser-only.

static_analysis.best_practice: postgres-language-server 0.27.0 (2026-10-04) is current and its release adds flat linter rule ids and static type checking - the capabilities the guide already describes and pins.
static_analysis.evidence: The pinned analyzer set is current at the exact version the guide names.
static_analysis.guide_position: postgres-language-server provides schema-aware completion, EXPLAIN-backed type checking and a safety linter; sqruff lint is the CI gate; sqls was evaluated and rejected with reasons recorded (pre-1.0, live-connection-centered).

testing.best_practice: Consistent with current PostgreSQL practice; the reference module for this guide passed 12 executed checks against a real server on 2026-10-14, evidencing the harness works as described.
testing.evidence: No testing-model change in the PostgreSQL 18 line affects the split or the corpus.
testing.guide_position: Real migrations against a real throwaway server (never an engine mock), from-empty and from-previous-release schema paths, half validation / half adversarial: injection corpus in every parameter, NULL storms, boundary cardinalities, type edges, and two-session concurrency races ending in designed outcomes; pgTAP or host-language harnesses both accepted.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Every pin except sqruff verifies exactly: PostgreSQL 18.6 / 2026-08-13 and the 14 end-of-life date match the official announcement and versioning policy, and postgres-language-server 0.27.0 (2026-10-04) is the latest release. The guide's source list still cites the 19 Beta 3 announcement while Beta 4 shipped 2026-09-24 (19 remains beta, so the 'not a target' ruling still holds).
toolchain_pins.evidence: No sqruff 0.41 release could be found: the latest verifiable sqruff crate releases are 0.40.0 (lib/lsp crates, 2026-08-14) and the main crate listing shows 0.39.0 (2026-07-03). The pin is therefore unverified rather than confirmed or refuted.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Primary target PostgreSQL 18 (17 supported), latest minor 18.6 of 2026-08-13, 14 end-of-life 2026-11-12, 19 beta not a target; postgres-language-server 0.27.0; sqruff '0.41 series' recorded as the crates.io line at review time.
